\subsection{CM family 20: Pack-face terminal obligations}
This family accounts for 71 branch obligations. Its proof rule is direct face failure; its terminal mechanism is carrier, cover, or Pack gauge failure routed by the row's face sort rule; its tested requirement is \(\Pack_Q\). The branch is read as Pack or Pack bridge.

\paragraph{CM obligation 910.}
The selected terminal mechanism is carrier, cover, or Pack gauge failure routed by the row's face sort rule. The tested requirement is \(\Pack_Q\). The proof rule is direct face failure. \emph{Claim.} \(B_{910}\Rightarrow\neg\Pack_Q\), hence \(B_{910}\Rightarrow\Exit(Q;\Owork)\). \emph{Proof.} A member branch must first carry \(Q\) by a positive same-fluid packet. The selected terminal branch loses that carrier requirement before any participation or field readout can be asked of it. The Pack-first order therefore gives \(\neg\Pack_Q\), and the class-exit embedding gives \(\Exit(Q;\Owork)\).

\subsection{CM family 28: support-boundary obligations}
This family accounts for 10 branch obligations. Its proof rule is support retained outside the CM conclusion until a bridge supplies a face; its terminal mechanism is carrier, cover, or Pack gauge failure routed by the row's face sort rule; its tested requirement is no independent Pack/Part/Field face. The branch is read as downstream export support.

\paragraph{CM obligation 1404.}
The selected terminal mechanism is carrier, cover, or Pack gauge failure routed by the row's face sort rule. The tested requirement is no independent Pack/Part/Field face. The proof rule is support retained outside the CM conclusion until a bridge supplies a face. \emph{Claim.} \(B_{1404}\) has no CM conclusion until it selects a same-fluid terminal packet. \emph{Proof.} A support branch can strengthen the positive pass side, sharpen a pressure test, or prepare a later terminal witness. \section{Expanded Forward-Support Obligations}

Forward-positive material enters the paper only after it is rewritten as support for a class-membership hinge. Each obligation below records the support role without letting forward progress substitute for the CM conclusion.

\subsection{Support family 1: demoted positive / export/legacy / supplier / readout / positive smoothness / transfer/Euler}
This family accounts for 24 support obligations. Its role is demoted positive-support language; downstream export or legacy-engine support; forward supplier support; receiver, readout, or endpoint support; separate positive-smoothness support; transfer or Euler-comparison support; it may support a CM hinge only through a Pack-first admission, a receiver/readout bridge, or a same-branch transfer license.

\paragraph{Support obligation 1.}
The support type is separate positive-smoothness support; forward supplier support; transfer or Euler-comparison support; receiver, readout, or endpoint support; downstream export or legacy-engine support; demoted positive-support language. \emph{Claim.} \(S_{1}\) enters the Navier--Stokes class proof only after it selects an exact same-fluid Navier--Stokes packet. \emph{Proof.} Comparison information may locate an analogous obstruction or exclude a misleading branch shape. \paragraph{Support obligation 787.}
The support type is separate positive-smoothness support; forward supplier support; receiver, readout, or endpoint support; downstream export or legacy-engine support; demoted positive-support language. \emph{Claim.} \(S_{787}\) has proof force through membership readout or through a Field-face loss. \emph{Proof.} A readout statement is downstream of the carrier and participation requirements. When the readout remains bounded on a positive scale, it supports the pass-side continuation norm. When every positive-scale readout fails, it supplies \(\forall r>0\,\neg\Field_{N,r,Q}\) and the fail side exits the class.

\section{Expanded Branch-Family Obligations}

The current-material coverage families are represented by mathematical proof roles rather than file names. Repetition is by branch family, so the visible appendix shows the obligation being carried instead of repeating the same anonymous sentence for every source item.

\paragraph{Branch-family obligation 1.}
\emph{Source-reserve family.} This family accounts for 41 current obligations. This branch family is tested by source survival, zero-radius refinement, signed-current/no-free-sink pressure, retained amplitude, and terminal atom mechanisms. \emph{Proof.} The proof first asks whether a positive same-fluid packet carries the source residue. Carrier loss gives \(\neg\Pack_Q\). A surviving carrier then asks whether the pressure-viscosity tower remains the same; failure gives \(\neg\Part_{N,Q}\). Surviving participation finally asks for a positive-scale coherent field readout; failure at every scale gives the Field face.

\paragraph{Branch-family obligation 2.}
\emph{Local translator family.} This family accounts for 3 current obligations. This family tests local critical translation as a same-solution packet question. \emph{Proof.} The translator has proof force only when it preserves the same Navier--Stokes pressure-viscosity participation on the transported packet. Loss of that participation is a Part-side failure; a surviving translator then moves to Field readout.

\paragraph{Branch-family obligation 3.}
\emph{Same-ledger family.} This family accounts for 8 current obligations. This family asks whether the terminal branch is still charged to the same witness record. \emph{Proof.} A terminal item on the same ledger enters the Pack-first test. A preterminal reflection or unpaid imported branch has no member conclusion until it supplies the same witness record, the same carrier, and the same participation tower.

\paragraph{Branch-family obligation 4.}
\emph{Class-law family.} This family accounts for 17 current obligations. This family tests the pass-or-exit law against possible reopening branches. \emph{Proof.} A reopening branch must either be an in-class nonsmooth third branch or break terminal CM entry, finite Pack/Part/Field exhaustion, or class-exit embedding. Every other challenge is absorbed by the installed pass branch, fail branch, or no-third-branch law.

\paragraph{Branch-family obligation 5.}
\emph{Local energy and elliptic family.} This family accounts for 3 current obligations. This family supplies analytic support for source-wall and classification tests. \emph{Proof.} Local energy and elliptic control matter when they select the terminal packet, verify pressure participation, or read out a positive field scale. The support is then consumed by Pack, Part, Field, or membership readout.

\paragraph{Branch-family obligation 6.}
\emph{Comparison-boundary family.} This family accounts for 7 current obligations. This family marks comparison branches that need an exact Navier--Stokes packet before entering the CM proof. \emph{Proof.} The comparison may reveal a useful branch shape. The proof uses it only after the Navier--Stokes witness record, carrier, participation, and field readout are stated for the same solution.

\paragraph{Branch-family obligation 7.}
\emph{Candidate-branch family.} This family accounts for 10 current obligations. This family contains candidate pressure tests and route probes. \emph{Proof.} A candidate becomes proof material only when it names a terminal packet and a requirement face. The face then routes through Pack, Part, Field, membership readout, terminal capture, or no-third-branch exclusion.
